name: Run Sensitivity Probe (test-audit-loop)
description: Periodic perturbation runner for the test-audit loop (OpenSpec 2026-05-18-test-audit-loop §C). Takes a test_registration, iterates over its perturbation_schedule, executes the registered test once per perturbation (applying the perturbation to the test's declared inputs), captures the resulting test_report, compares observed vs predicted outcome, and emits one sensitivity_evidence impulse per (test, perturbation, run) triple. Aggregated over the trailing ≥7-day window the evidence drives audit-test-report's check_sensitivity_evidence task (insensitive-test detection). Default cadence is weekly via the existing weekly cron at validation/scripts/run-weekly-harness.sh; registrations may override via perturbation_cadence ∈ {daily, weekly, monthly}. Triggered immediately on lifecycle:test_registration:updated so a modified test is re-probed without waiting for the next cycle.

variables.name: test_registration_id
variables.description: Test id (test_registration.id) of the registration to probe. The weekly cron supplies one of these per registered test per dispatch; ad-hoc invocations (workbench, lifecycle:test_registration:updated handler) supply it directly.

variables.name: run_id_prefix
variables.description: Prefix for the run_id stamped on each emitted sensitivity_evidence row. Defaults to 'probe'; harness invocations may override with 'weekly-{date}' to make the trailing-window query deterministic per cron tick.

tasks.description: Read the test_registration to probe — needed for the perturbation_schedule and the inputs_schema (so the perturbation_application step knows how to map input_path to a concrete location in the test's input variables).
tasks.notes: Uses the new test_registration read shape (Phase A). When the registration is missing, the read returns an empty entries[] and the downstream iteration short-circuits with maxIterations=0; no perturbations execute, no evidence is emitted.

tasks.description: Iterate over the registration's perturbation_schedule, executing the perturbed test once per entry and recording per-perturbation outcomes.

variables._note: The dispatched test reads the __perturbation_apply block to mutate its declared inputs per Perturbation.apply.{ input_path, transform }. Transforms recognised by the perturbation-application helper resolver: set_to_existing (replaces with an arbitrary existing-but-different value drawn from the live registry), unset (deletes the field), set:<value> (overrides with the literal value after the colon).

tasks.notes: The iteration body dispatches the registered test as an activity (templateId = test_registration.id, since tests are activities with output_shapes: ['test_report'] per design.md §E.1). The __perturbation_apply variable carries the transform spec the perturbation-application helper resolver (registered separately per tasks.md C.1.2) reads to mutate the test's declared inputs before execution. stopOnError=false ensures one failing perturbation does not abort the probe — each iteration's outcome (success/failure/error) becomes an observed_effect on the per-iteration sensitivity_evidence row.

tasks.description: For each (perturbation, observed test_report) pair, compare observed_effect to perturbation.expected_effect and emit one sensitivity_evidence row via the sensitivity_evidence_write resolver. varied_as_predicted is true iff (expected_effect, observed_effect) match the predicted direction; numerical expected_delta vs observed_delta carries the magnitude for audit-test-report's downstream insensitive/noisy classification.
tasks.notes: The __derived_from_iteration_outcome__ / __derived__ placeholders mark fields that need a tiny deterministic post-step the dispatch resolver runs before forwarding: observed_effect is computed from iteration_outcome.status (pass/fail) and the test_report's assertion verdict; varied_as_predicted is the boolean match against perturbation.expected_effect; observed_delta is derived from the per-test metric when the report carries one (else null). Until that post-step is fully wired in the iteration resolver, callers can pre-compute and inject the derived fields via a synthesise_evidence_rows resolver — the schema (SensitivityEvidenceSchema) tolerates either path. The aggregation result is the list of emitted ids, available to downstream audit-test-report dispatches that follow this probe.

metadata.author: test-audit-loop
metadata.cadenceContract: Default cadence is weekly via validation/scripts/run-weekly-harness.sh (Phase G). Registrations may override via test_registration.perturbation_cadence ∈ {daily, weekly, monthly}; cadence changes (or any testRegistration_write) fire lifecycle:test_registration:updated which triggers an immediate probe on the next dispatch tick (spec Requirement R3).
metadata.evidenceContract: Emits one sensitivity_evidence impulse per (test, perturbation, run) triple. audit-test-report's check_sensitivity_evidence task queries the trailing ≥7-day window with ≥3 runs per perturbation. Below the window, audit-test-report tags the report with caveat 'missing_sensitivity_history' rather than failing — the probe is build-up history, not gate.
metadata.perturbationTransforms: perturbation.apply.transform values recognised: 'set_to_existing' (replace with another existing value drawn from the live registry, useful for swapping missing_shape → existing_shape per the worked example in design.md §I), 'unset' (delete the field, e.g. unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), 'set:<literal>' (override with the literal after the colon, e.g. set:0.10 for budget_usd). Extensions land via the perturbation-application helper resolver per tasks.md C.1.2.
